name: Mobile app
when: Phone-first apps and mobile web apps: short sessions, one hand, interruptions, unreliable connections.

actors.who: Someone using the app in short bursts between other things, often one-handed.
questions: Which task do they open the app for most, and how long is a typical session?
Where are they when they use it: walking, commuting, at a counter, at home?
How reliable is their connection, and what should happen when it drops mid-task?
Which phone sizes and operating system versions do they use?
What interrupts them, and what do they expect to find when they come back?

actors.who: Someone who just installed the app and is deciding in the first minute whether to keep it.
questions: What did they install it for, in their own words?
What are they willing to give before seeing value: an account, permissions, notifications?
What makes them uninstall in the first session?

screens.name: Onboarding
screens.does: Gets to the first useful screen with as little setup as possible.

screens.name: Permission request
screens.does: Understands why a permission is asked before deciding.

screens.name: Home
screens.does: Starts the task they opened the app for, within thumb reach.

screens.name: List
screens.does: Scans and opens an item; pulls to refresh.

screens.name: Detail
screens.does: Reads one item and takes its main action.

screens.name: Form
screens.does: Enters data with the right keyboard and without losing it to an interruption.

screens.name: Offline or error state
screens.does: Knows what happened and what still works without a connection.

journeys.goal: Reach the first useful screen after installing
watch: Count the steps and fields before the first useful screen; each must earn its place.
A permission is asked when its feature is first used, with the reason on screen.
Skipping a permission still leads somewhere useful.

journeys.goal: Do the task the app is opened for
watch: The primary action on each screen is within thumb reach without scrolling at 390x844.
Every tap answers within a second; anything longer shows progress.
Going back returns to the same place in the list.

journeys.goal: Finish a form after an interruption or a lost connection
watch: What was typed is still there after the error or the interruption.
The offline state says what failed and offers to retry.
Each field brings up the keyboard its answer needs.

research: Which task opens the app most often, and how long does it take today?
What share of sessions start from a notification, a link or the home screen?
Which platform conventions do users expect here (back gestures, tab bars, share sheets)?
Which store reviews of this app and its competitors complain about what?
What data must stay on the device or work offline, and what do privacy rules require for it?

sources.name: Apple Human Interface Guidelines
sources.why: Platform conventions iOS users expect: navigation, controls, permissions, layout.

sources.name: Material Design 3
sources.why: Platform conventions Android users expect, with component usage guidance.

sources.name: Nielsen Norman Group — 10 usability heuristics
sources.why: The baseline vocabulary for reviewing any screen.

sources.name: WCAG 2.2 — target size
sources.why: The minimum touch target size and spacing a phone screen must meet.
